transcript: Last night, I saw a lovely new play by Kelly Jones called My Mother's Funeral: The Show. It's currently being presented at Soho Playhouse as part of their International Fringe Encore Series and there's no shortage of exciting downtown theater especially with it also being festival season in New York. My Mother's Funeral is kind of hard to describe, but basically our protagonist Abigail has just lost her mother and she can't afford the funeral so she writes a play about that very predicament. It’s a cool mix of comedy, tragedy, meta commentary and some semi-fourth-wall-breaking moments. For a 70-minute economically staged one-act with a cast of three, this multi dimensional show packs a lot of ideas. I primarily interpreted it as a critique on what it takes to create art that's personal, and the dissonance between what that costs the artist and what can be gained. Overall, I thought this was a thoughtful and entertaining piece that should resonate with anyone who's a creative. My Mother's Funeral is running through January 25th at Soho Playbouse. With that, another program for my collection.
